content:
The late Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, has spoken out about the ongoing rift between Princes William and Harry.

In an interview with the BBC, Spencer said: "I think there's a perception in the media that I am on Harry's side. Actually, I am on the side of my late sister's two sons — I support them both." The interview aired on Sunday to coincide with the release of his new book about Diana, *Swan Song: My Sister Diana*.

The historian added: "Whatever either of them needs, I will support equally. I never take sides; I just want to be a positive figure."

Speaking about the broken relationship between Harry and William, Spencer said things had "reached this point" and that "there are many reasons on both sides."

He said: "I hope it can be resolved one day, but I don't know the full picture. I'm certainly not aware of all the details, so I feel it would be presumptuous of me to get too involved. I can only say that any mother would surely want her two sons to get along happily and love each other."

In a separate interview with *People* magazine, Spencer addressed another topic likely to interest royal watchers: when he told the two brothers about the book.

Spencer said: "I told them at the same time. I can say that one... so all four of them — William, Harry, and my two sisters Sarah and Jane — I told them at exactly the same time. Harry had absolutely no problem with it."

He shared: "[Harry] said he hoped the book wouldn't contain anything embarrassing about him. I said: 'No.' I think they were both a little worried about where my book might go." He added that the book "essentially ends with Diana's death in 1997."

He said: "But I can assure both of them that they will, of course, appear in the book — though primarily as examples of two young boys with an extraordinary mother. I would never intrude on their privacy in any way."

Spencer's new book was published on Tuesday, marking the 30th anniversary of Diana's death on 31 August 1997.
